## Readable multiline prompt text

TrainLens prompt recipes often accept longer free-form instructions such as `objective`. Until now, examples had to split those instructions into many adjacent quoted strings just to keep Python source lines readable. That adds visual noise, slows down prompt editing, and makes notebook cells look less like the prose users are actually trying to write.

TrainLens 0.14.1 adds `prompt_text()` so those instructions can be written as normal triple-quoted multiline text. The helper removes common code indentation and surrounding blank space while preserving relative indentation inside the prompt.

```python
from trainlens import improvement_plan_prompt, prompt_text

prompt = improvement_plan_prompt(
    objective=prompt_text("""
        Explain what happened during this fine-tuning run and propose the three
        highest-value next experiments.

        Use the test split only as final generalization evidence; do not tune to it.
        Prefer controlled, low-cost changes first.
    """),
)
```

This release also updates the README and Colab quickstart to use the new workflow and adds tests covering multiline dedenting and whitespace cleanup.
